summary: Roadmap item 6 of dimension32-global-topology: how A_5 partner spheres specialize across the 33 closure incidences 8 -> 12, 12 -> 16 and 8 -> 16, as closed kernel Gauss-graph fibers with two-sided real certificates and attaching maps, run as a Codex program.

reconciliation.note: Captured context; triage and evidence review pending.

scope: Evidence bundle docs/evidence/a5-kernel-attachments (scripts, records, README, ledger) and the program file docs/design/a5-kernel-attachments-program.md; the 33 incidences between the nullity-8, nullity-12 and nullity-16 orbits. next_action: Run the Codex program from the program file; review and commit each sub-step.

steps.action: Enumerate all 33 incidences with exact boundary points, moved points included, and decide per incidence whether the first-order effective form on the boundary kernel is complex-linear in the normal direction.
steps.acceptance: Fails if a declared incidence lacks an exact verified point or a second boundary point reverses a complex-linearity verdict without explanation.

steps.action: Compute the closed Gauss-graph fiber in Gr(4,6) for every 8 -> 12 incidence with an exact upper bound and filling exact real arcs, and its variation over the boundary moduli.
steps.acceptance: Fails if an exact arc limit escapes the upper bound, a point of the bound is reached by no certified arc, or a moved boundary point changes the set beyond the stated variation.

steps.action: The same for the 8 incidences 12 -> 16 and the 10 incidences 8 -> 16, starting with a two-approach path-dependence test.
steps.acceptance: Fails on the same criteria as the 8 -> 12 step.

steps.action: Compare limits composed through nullity 12 with the direct 8 -> 16 limit sets.
steps.acceptance: Fails if a composed limit lies outside the direct limit set or the reverse inclusion is claimed without arcs.

steps.action: Describe the link-to-limit-set maps and the sphere-union maps into the boundary partner sphere with their homotopy data in a form a global model can assemble.
steps.acceptance: Fails if a stated homotopy datum is neither computed by a replayed producer nor labeled as an argument.
